title: TechMind AI Challenge
rules: Participation is allowed individually or in a team of maximum two students.
Only three prompts per round are permitted.
Permitted tools include ChatGPT, OpenAI Tools, Google Gemini and other AI-based platforms.
Plagiarism or duplication of ideas results in immediate disqualification.
Judges’ decision is final and binding.
guide: Choose individual or a two-student team.
Prepare to work with permitted AI tools.
Use no more than three prompts in each round.
Create original work and avoid duplicated ideas.
Follow the judges’ instructions throughout the challenge.

title: Void Run
rules: Each team can contain a minimum of 1 and maximum of 4 persons.
Teams may bring their own laptop to perform the game.
AI and internet use is allowed during the starting round.
Teams must not tamper with game files, LAN network or another team’s system.
The winner is decided on the basis of the leaderboard.
guide: Register as an individual or team of up to four.
Bring your own laptop if needed for the game.
Use AI/internet only as permitted for the starting round.
Do not modify game files, LAN systems or another team’s setup.
Follow the leaderboard-based result and coordinator instructions.

title: BRIDGE WARS
rules: The bridge model must have a clear span of 30 cm.
Maximum cross-section is 15 cm × 15 cm.
The bridge must be fabricated entirely at the venue; prefabricated or pre-assembled components are not permitted.
Participants must bring the specified materials: ice-cream sticks and Fevicol.
The completed bridge is tested by applying load at the designated central loading point.
Winner selection considers maximum load-carrying capacity, structural efficiency, innovation and overall design.
guide: Form a team of up to 3 members.
Bring ice-cream sticks and Fevicol as specified.
Build the bridge at the competition venue.
Keep the 30 cm clear span and 15 cm × 15 cm maximum cross-section in mind.
Submit the finished model for the central load test.

title: Electrical Masters
guide: Use the registration information supplied by the organizers.
Confirm the round structure, equipment requirements and detailed rules with the faculty coordinator before participating.
Arrive with the materials or equipment specifically instructed by the organizers.

title: RoboFootball League
rules: The uploaded rules document is titled RoboFootball League, but its table names the event RoboChrono Challenge.
An electric-powered robot is provided to each participant to complete the given track.
Each participant gets only one chance to complete the track.
The participant who takes less time to complete the task is the winner.
No test practice is allowed.
The organizer has the right to take the final decision on event matters.
The referee’s decision is final.
guide: Confirm the exact RoboFootball/RoboChrono format with the coordinator because the supplied documents use different names.
Use the electric-powered robot provided by the organizers if the supplied rules apply.
Be ready for one timed attempt and no practice run.
Focus on completing the track quickly and follow referee instructions.

title: Clay Modeling
rules: Eligibility: open to registered institute participants/students.
The model must follow the theme announced by organizers.
Participants must complete the model within the allotted time; the rules give 2 hours as an example.
Clay will be provided or participants may bring their own as specified.
Basic modelling tools may be used; sharp or hazardous tools are not permitted.
The work must be original and created during the competition.
Participants must work independently.
Keep the work area clean and follow safety instructions.
Submit/display the completed model at the designated place before time ends.
Judging: creativity and originality 25%; relevance to theme 20%; artistic presentation 20%; skill and finishing 20%; overall impact 15%.
Prohibited materials, copying, outside assistance or rule violations may lead to disqualification.
Judges’ decision is final and binding.
Organizers may modify rules, schedule or arrangements if necessary.
guide: Register for the event.
Check the announced theme and required clay/material arrangement.
Prepare basic safe modelling tools.
Create the model independently within the allotted time.
Keep your area clean and submit/display the finished model before time expires.
Make the design original and aligned with the theme.

title: Vision Board – Poster Presentation
rules: The poster must relate to the given theme/topic.
The poster must be handmade; printed posters are not accepted.
Poster size: minimum 1 ft × 1 ft and maximum 2 ft × 2 ft.
Lettering and images must be readable from a minimum distance of 2 feet.
Official poster languages: Marathi, English or Hindi.
Participants must explain the poster within 3–5 minutes.
Offensive or copied content is strictly prohibited.
Judging is based on creativity, clarity, content and presentation skills.
guide: Prepare a handmade poster around the announced topic/theme.
Keep the poster between 1×1 ft and 2×2 ft.
Use Marathi, English or Hindi.
Make text and visuals readable from at least 2 feet.
Prepare a clear 3–5 minute explanation.
Use original, respectful content.

title: Cipher Chase
rules: Solo or group of 3 participants is allowed.
All participants must follow instructions and time limits of each round.
Mobile phones, internet and outside assistance are not allowed unless permitted by coordinators.
Cheating, unfair means or misconduct results in disqualification.
Participants must maintain discipline and respectful behaviour.
Judges’ and event coordinators’ decision is final and binding.
guide: Choose solo participation or a 3-member group.
Follow each round’s instructions and time limit.
Do not use mobile/internet or outside help unless explicitly permitted.
Solve the cipher/challenge independently and maintain discipline.
Follow coordinator and judge decisions.

title: TECH TREASURE HUNT – “The Digital Heist”
rules: Each team consists of 2 students.
The event has 3 rounds.
Round 1: solve the given code; its output gives the clue/location for Round 2.
Round 2: find and solve the puzzle at the given location; its output is the password for the designated PC.
Round 3: teams completing Round 2 proceed to the Surprise Round.
Each round must be completed within the given time limit.
Mobile phones, internet and external help are not allowed unless organizers permit them.
Sharing clues, answers or helping other teams is prohibited.
Organizers’/judges’ decision is final and binding.
guide: Create a 2-student team.
Start by solving the code in Round 1.
Use the output as the clue/location for Round 2.
Solve the location puzzle and use its output as the designated PC password.
Qualify for and complete the Surprise Round.
Respect time limits and do not share clues or answers.

title: CAD MASTER 2K26
rules: Individual participation is permitted.
Report to the venue at least 15 minutes before the scheduled start.
The challenge tests CADD skills related to Civil Engineering.
A drawing/problem statement is given at the beginning.
Complete the drawing/design within the specified time.
Use only software/systems provided or approved by the organizing committee.
Pre-prepared drawings, templates, external files, mobile phones, internet resources and unauthorized materials are prohibited.
Save work periodically and submit the final drawing in the specified format.
Do not communicate or exchange files with other participants.
Malpractice or copying results in immediate disqualification.
Report technical problems immediately to the event coordinator.
Extra time may be provided only at the committee’s discretion.
Judges’ and organizing committee’s decision is final and binding.
Maintain discipline, dignity and professional conduct.
guide: Participate individually.
Reach the venue at least 15 minutes early.
Use only approved systems/software.
Start from the drawing/problem statement given at the event.
Save your work regularly and submit it in the required format.
Do not use prepared templates/files, internet, phones or unauthorized aids.
Immediately report technical issues to the coordinator.

guide: Participate as a team of maximum 2 members.
Handle laboratory equipment carefully and do not modify/damage it.
Check whether internet/electronic devices are permitted before each round.

title: Mech Creo Challenge
rules: Carry a valid college/student ID card.
Follow instructions from coordinators and volunteers.
Mobile phones, smart watches, calculators, books, notes and unauthorized aids are not permitted unless specifically allowed.
Cheating, communication with other teams or outside assistance results in immediate disqualification.
Event Coordinator/Judging Committee decision is final and binding.
Organizers may modify rules, timings or round sequence if required.

Round 1 – Memory Game: observe images/objects/symbols/numbers/components for a limited time, then answer identification, position, count, matching, missing-object or sequence questions. Display/question timing is 30–60 seconds as specified.
Round 2 – Error Detective: identify faults in diagrams, machine arrangements, drawings, workshop situations, components or technical images; explain or suggest solutions where asked.
Final Round – Treasure Hunt: solve a series of clues/tasks involving mechanical concepts, workshop equipment, symbols, components, puzzles, locations or observation tasks. Teams must remain together.
Do not disturb equipment, run in unsafe areas, remove/damage/hide clues or interfere with another team.
Hints may carry a penalty according to organizer rules.
Disqualification may result from cheating, unauthorized devices, tampering, property damage, restricted-area entry, unsafe behaviour or misconduct.
guide: Carry your college/student ID.
Prepare for three stages: Memory Game, Error Detective and Treasure Hunt.
For Memory Game, focus on observation and recall within the short display/question windows.
For Error Detective, identify the fault and give an explanation/solution when required.
For Treasure Hunt, stay together, solve clues in sequence and follow safety rules.
Do not use unauthorized aids or interfere with equipment/clues.
note: The source rules use the spelling “Mech Creo Challange”; the event-plan and summary sheet use “Mech Creo Challenge.”

title: Brain Byte
rules: The quiz has two rounds.
Each team consists of 2 participants.
Round 1 covers technical knowledge and may include MCQs and general technical questions.
Round 2 is a Rapid Fire/Buzzer round where quick and accurate answers are rewarded.
Answer within the time limit for each question.
Quiz Master and Judges’ decision is final and binding.
Teams violating rules may be disqualified.
guide: Create a 2-member team.
Prepare technical knowledge and general technical questions.
Practice quick responses for the Rapid Fire/Buzzer round.
Answer within the allotted time and follow the Quiz Master’s instructions.
